description: The bar chart illustrates the performance of three LLaMA-2 models—LLaMA-2-7B, LLaMA-2-13B, and LLaMA-2-70B—on the CoLeG-R benchmark, measured as percentage accuracy, under four different fine-tuning conditions: no SFT (supervised fine-tuning), SFT on dataset D₀ only, SFT on datasets D₀ and D₁, and SFT on datasets D₀, D₁, and D₂. The vertical axis represents CoLeG-R (%) ranging from 0 to 80 in increments of 10, while the horizontal axis lists the three model sizes. Each model has four bars grouped together, colored and patterned as follows: light blue with diagonal stripes for “no SFT”, light orange with horizontal stripes for “+ SFT on D₀”, light purple with diagonal stripes for “+ SFT on D₀, D₁”, and light red with solid fill for “+ SFT on D₀, D₁, D₂”. For LLaMA-2-7B, performance increases from ~67% (no SFT) to ~83% (SFT on all three datasets). For LLaMA-2-13B, scores rise from ~70% to ~84%. For LLaMA-2-70B, performance improves from ~80% to ~83%, showing diminishing returns at the largest scale. Across all models, adding more datasets for SFT consistently improves performance, with the largest gains observed between “no SFT” and “+ SFT on D₀”, and smaller incremental gains thereafter. The chart visually emphasizes that larger models benefit from SFT but plateau sooner, while smaller models show more relative improvement with additional training data.
